title.narrative: Global WASH Program(GWP) Phase II, Zimbabwe

description.narrative: Direct Beneficiaries:(1) Micro Level (Community and Service Providers): 480 community members are reached through District WASH Master Plan (DWMP) advocacy and inclusive planning efforts. 40 individuals are engaged in piloting the Community-Based Management (CBM) model, including tool testing and training. 120 water service users benefit from participatory feedback mechanisms supporting accountability and improved WASH governance.(2) Meso Level (District Level): Six districts establish and implement DWMPs. 15 district stakeholders in Mount Darwin and Chegutu are trained in CBM model implementation. Three officials receive training in MIS development and management. Ten government stakeholders improve their community engagement capacities through public campaigns.(3) Macro Level (Provincial and National): Five national WASH coordination members and DNWASH Co actors deepen their understanding of DWMP and CBM for scale-up. Thirty working group members and 30 macro-level stakeholders are trained in WASH systems building blocks. Ten provincial facilitators are trained in coordination and monitoring. Five NGOs and development partners are oriented in WASH system strengthening.Indirect Beneficiaries:(1) Micro Level: 10,000 community members reached with awareness materials. 10,000 additional users benefit from improved water services and dialogue platforms resulting from CBM efforts;(2) Meso Level: Eight additional districts initiate DWMP replication. 377,740 households benefit from strengthened WASH services. 1,440 meso-level actors indirectly benefit from training on improved management models;(3) Macro Level: Ten provinces are exposed to DWMP guidelines and prepared to replicate the model. Four provinces are influenced by WASH-related policies and strategies. 1.5 million households benefit from national-level policy reforms and advocacy outcomes.

In Zimbabwe, Phase II of the Global WASH Programme (GWP) supports transformative change across three interconnected outcomes: Service Delivery Strengthening, Integrated Inclusive Planning, and Accountability and Monitoring—each reinforcing sustainable, equitable rural WASH systems.

This project is part of Phase II of the Global WASH Program (GWP) implemented in Sierra Leone, Zimbabwe, Pakistan and India. Building on Phase I, Phase II of the program focuses on scaling and institutionalizing WASH systems strengthening across five key areas: Service Delivery Strengthening, Inclusive Planning, Accountability & Monitoring, Institutional Arrangements & Coordination, and Learning & Sector Adaptation. A key emphasis is the shift from systems strengthening to systems delivery, ensuring sustainable WASH services for target communities. Phase II embeds these approaches in government structures and policies, reducing dependency on external support. Advocacy and stakeholder collaboration remain vital for financial sustainability and institutional adaptation.
